moduleInfo.title: God's Rules for Love: The 10 Commandments
moduleInfo.subject: Religion/Catechism

vocabulary.term: I am the LORD your God: you shall not have strange gods before me.
vocabulary.definition: Put God first in your life and worship only Him.

vocabulary.term: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain.
vocabulary.definition: Show respect for God's name and all holy things; do not use His name carelessly or angrily.

vocabulary.term: Remember to keep holy the LORD’s Day.
vocabulary.definition: Go to Mass on Sundays and holy days, and use the day for rest, family, and prayer.

vocabulary.term: Honor your father and your mother.
vocabulary.definition: Love, obey, and respect your parents, guardians, and other lawful authorities.
Respect all human life from beginning to end; do not hurt others with your body or unkind words.
Respect the sacrament of marriage and treat your own body and the bodies of others with modesty and respect.
Respect the things that belong to others; do not take, damage, or cheat to get something that is not yours.

vocabulary.term: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
vocabulary.definition: Always tell the truth, and do not lie or spread rumors that harm another person's good name.

vocabulary.term: You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife.
vocabulary.definition: Be pure in your thoughts and desires; do not wish for something that belongs to someone else's family.

vocabulary.term: You shall not covet your neighbor’s goods.
vocabulary.definition: Be thankful for what you have and do not be jealous of the possessions of others.
Another word for the Ten Commandments.
Worshipping anything or anyone other than God.
Deep respect for someone or something.
Telling secrets or rumors, especially if they are untrue or unkind.
Listening to and doing what parents or teachers ask.

artworks.title: The Golden Rule
artworks.description: The teaching to treat others the way you want to be treated.

artworks.title: The Two Great Commandments
artworks.description: Jesus’ summary of all the laws: love God and love your neighbor.

artworks.title: The Catechism of the Catholic Church
artworks.description: The official summary of Catholic faith and morals.

artworks.title: The Gift of Life
artworks.description: The belief that every person's life is special and comes from God.

artworks.title: The Virtue of Charity
artworks.description: The Christian habit of loving God above all things and loving your neighbor as yourself.

artworks.title: The Sacrament of Holy Matrimony
artworks.description: The special way God blesses the love between a husband and wife.

artworks.title: The Virtue of Honesty
artworks.description: The practice of always telling the truth and respecting others' reputations.

artworks.title: Gratitude
artworks.description: Being thankful for the things you have instead of being jealous of others.

locations.name: Mount Sinai
locations.significance: The place where God gave the Ten Commandments to Moses.

locations.name: The Church
locations.significance: The place where Catholics keep the Lord's Day holy by attending Mass.

locations.name: Home
locations.significance: The first and most important place where children learn to honor their parents.

locations.name: School
locations.significance: A place where children practice honesty, respect for property, and kindness to their neighbors.

locations.name: The Vatican
locations.significance: The home of the Pope, the chief teacher of the Catholic faith, which explains the Commandments.

locations.name: The Heart
locations.significance: The spiritual place where we decide to love or covet, and where God's law is written.

locations.name: Heaven
locations.significance: The final goal for those who follow God's Commandments on earth.

locations.name: Egypt
locations.significance: The land from which God freed the Israelites before giving them the Commandments.

locations.name: The Garden of Eden
locations.significance: The place where God first created human life, which the Fifth Commandment protects.

locations.name: The Bible
locations.significance: The book where the story of Moses receiving the Commandments is found.

locations.name: Any Parish
locations.significance: A local Catholic community where people gather to worship and learn God's rules.

locations.name: Your Conscience
locations.significance: The inner voice that tells you right from wrong, helping you follow the Commandments.

locations.name: The Neighborhood
locations.significance: The area where we treat our 'neighbor' with respect and truthfulness.

locations.name: The Confessional
locations.significance: The place where Catholics receive forgiveness for breaking the Commandments.

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.significance: The city where Jesus taught the importance of loving God and neighbor.

trueFalse.statement: The First Commandment teaches us to put our favorite video game before going to church.
trueFalse.correction: The First Commandment teaches us to put God first and worship only Him, not video games or other things.

trueFalse.statement: Using God’s name when you are angry is a way of keeping the Second Commandment.
trueFalse.correction: The Second Commandment says not to take God's name in vain; we must use His name with reverence and respect.

trueFalse.statement: The Third Commandment asks us to attend Mass on Sunday and treat the day as special.
trueFalse.correction: Attending Mass and resting from unnecessary work are ways to keep the Lord's Day holy.

trueFalse.statement: The Fourth Commandment is only about obeying your mother and father when you are a baby.
trueFalse.correction: The Fourth Commandment says to honor your parents, which means respecting and obeying them even as you grow older.

trueFalse.statement: The Fifth Commandment means you should never punch or hit someone, even if you are very angry.
trueFalse.correction: The Fifth Commandment protects life, which includes avoiding physical harm and hurtful words to others.

trueFalse.statement: The Sixth Commandment is mainly about showing love and respect in marriage.
trueFalse.correction: The Sixth Commandment is about respecting the commitment of marriage and being chaste.

trueFalse.statement: If you borrow a friend's pencil and forget to give it back, you are breaking the Seventh Commandment.
trueFalse.correction: The Seventh Commandment forbids stealing and requires us to respect the property of others, including returning borrowed items.

trueFalse.statement: Gossip and telling lies about your neighbor are fine, as long as it's only a small lie.
trueFalse.correction: The Eighth Commandment requires us to always tell the truth and protect our neighbor's good name.

trueFalse.statement: The Ninth and Tenth Commandments are special because they focus on our thoughts and feelings.
trueFalse.correction: These commandments teach us to control our inner desires and avoid jealousy and coveting.

trueFalse.statement: It is okay to cheat on a test as long as you promise to study harder next time.
trueFalse.correction: Cheating is a form of stealing (Seven/Eighth Commandment violation) because it is dishonest and taking a grade you did not earn.

trueFalse.statement: You honor your parents when you help with chores without being asked.
trueFalse.correction: Showing respect and obedience by helping out without being reminded is a way to honor parents.

trueFalse.statement: Wishing you had your friend's new bicycle instead of your old one is a sign of coveting.
trueFalse.correction: Coveting means being jealous or wishing for what belongs to another person, which breaks the Tenth Commandment.

trueFalse.statement: Respecting your body and avoiding unhealthy habits fulfills the positive meaning of the Fifth Commandment.
trueFalse.correction: The Fifth Commandment also includes taking care of our own life and health.

trueFalse.statement: If a teacher asks you to be quiet, you only have to obey if you agree with the reason.
trueFalse.correction: The Fourth Commandment to honor your parents extends to obeying lawful superiors like teachers, regardless of your personal agreement.

trueFalse.statement: We keep the Lord’s Day holy by spending the whole day buying new things at the mall.
trueFalse.correction: The Lord’s Day should be focused on God (Mass) and rest, not unnecessary work or excessive shopping.

quiz.question: Sarah spends all her allowance on a new figurine and starts praying to it, saying it brings her good luck. Which Commandment is she breaking?
options: I am the LORD your God: you shall not have strange gods before me.
Honor your father and your mother.
quiz.correctAnswer: I am the LORD your God: you shall not have strange gods before me.

quiz.question: When Mike got angry, he shouted out God's name carelessly in frustration. Which Commandment did he break?
options: Remember to keep holy the LORD’s Day.
You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
quiz.correctAnswer: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain.

quiz.question: It's Sunday, and Maria’s family decides to skip Mass to go to a theme park instead. Which Commandment did they fail to keep?
options: Honor your father and your mother.
You shall not covet your neighbor’s goods.
Remember to keep holy the LORD’s Day.
quiz.correctAnswer: Remember to keep holy the LORD’s Day.

quiz.question: Tom's mom asked him to clean his room, but he pretended he didn't hear her and went to play video games. Which Commandment is he disrespecting?
options: Honor your father and your mother.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife.
quiz.correctAnswer: Honor your father and your mother.

quiz.question: During recess, some kids started making fun of a new student, calling him mean names until he cried. Which Commandment are they going against?
options: You shall not covet your neighbor’s goods.
You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
quiz.correctAnswer: You shall not kill.

quiz.question: Jane found a \$ 5 bill on the floor of the classroom and decided to keep it without asking the teacher if anyone lost it. Which Commandment does this relate to?
options: You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife.
Remember to keep holy the LORD’s Day.
quiz.correctAnswer: You shall not steal.

quiz.question: When the principal asked who broke the window, Ben lied and said his friend Alex did it, to avoid getting in trouble himself. Which Commandment did Ben break?
options: You shall not covet your neighbor’s goods.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
Honor your father and your mother.
quiz.correctAnswer: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

quiz.question: Lisa saw her friend's new shoes and wished they were hers, feeling unhappy with her own old shoes. Which Commandment is her thought breaking?
options: Honor your father and your mother.
You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain.
You shall not covet your neighbor’s goods.
quiz.correctAnswer: You shall not covet your neighbor’s goods.

quiz.question: A newly married couple promises to always be faithful to each other. Which Commandment helps them keep this special promise?
options: Remember to keep holy the LORD’s Day.
quiz.correctAnswer: You shall not commit adultery.

quiz.question: What is the primary positive action commanded by 'I am the LORD your God: you shall not have strange gods before me'?
quiz.correctAnswer: Worshipping only God.

quiz.question: If you are playing a game and someone cheats, they are breaking the spirit of which Commandment?
options: Remember to keep holy the LORD’s Day.
Honor your father and your mother.
quiz.correctAnswer: You shall not steal.

quiz.question: What is the best way a child can practice 'Honor your father and your mother'?
options: Obeying them with a cheerful heart.
Only talking to them when they are happy.
Arguing until they get their way.
quiz.correctAnswer: Obeying them with a cheerful heart.

quiz.question: The Commandments that deal with loving God directly are the first how many?
quiz.correctAnswer: Three

quiz.question: The Commandments that focus on loving your neighbor are the last how many?
quiz.correctAnswer: Seven

quiz.question: What is another name for the Ten Commandments?
quiz.correctAnswer: The Decalogue

quiz.question: Which Commandment asks us to be thankful for what we have instead of being jealous of others' possessions?
quiz.correctAnswer: The Tenth Commandment

quiz.question: Which of these is a way to respect the Fifth Commandment ('You shall not kill') in everyday life?
options: Being kind and speaking gently to others.
quiz.correctAnswer: Being kind and speaking gently to others.

quiz.question: If you spread a false rumor about a classmate, which Commandment have you broken?
options: You shall not covet your neighbor’s goods.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
Remember to keep holy the LORD’s Day.
quiz.correctAnswer: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

quiz.question: How do you 'keep holy' the Lord's Day according to the Third Commandment?
options: By doing all your homework on Sunday.
By attending Mass and setting time aside for rest and family.
By playing video games all day.
By only thinking about God for five minutes.
quiz.correctAnswer: By attending Mass and setting time aside for rest and family.

quiz.question: Which Commandment encourages you to respect your own life and health?
quiz.correctAnswer: The Fifth Commandment
